task_name: Ironwood Kitchen - Product launch video package
client_brief:
Ironwood Kitchen is introducing the lunch range and we want it cut short and honest. What came back from the kitchen is one five second take, which is nowhere near a film, so the completed source pack adds the missing coverage and a cleared instrumental bed before anyone starts editing. Nothing here is narrated. These play muted in a feed and on the site, so the words sit on screen and the bed does the rest.

Please build a 12 to 15 second launch film in 16:9, cut from at least five different supplied video takes, and an 8 to 10 second upright cutdown that puts one complete bowl from the eight bowl stills on screen inside the first two seconds. No bowl shot in either film shows a grey reference card. Both carry the supplied bed, both close on the Ironwood Kitchen wordmark, and both show the price “$12” exactly as ironwood_skus.csv has it, beside the name of a bowl the film shows, with that bowl's allergen and macro line from the same sheet. Keep the claims to the two cleared lines in ironwood_notes.txt, the protein per bowl and the no added sugar in dressings, set word for word as written there; a named bowl's own name, description, allergen and macro figures from ironwood_skus.csv, the tagline “Real lunch, in the case by half ten” and the counter and route times in ironwood_notes.txt count as records, not claims. Anything past those two lines is not approved and we will send it back.

The eight bowl product modules, the two page lunch range line sheet and the film cover are handled separately and are not part of this delivery; both films draw on the same eight bowls.

brand_identity.tagline: Real lunch, in the case by half ten
brand_identity.sector: Fast casual grab and go: high protein meal prep bowls sold from a counter case and by office park delivery.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019, Providence, Rhode Island, two counters and three office park delivery routes run by a small kitchen crew.
brand_identity.about: Ironwood Kitchen builds honest, high protein bowls for the office lunch run, in the fridge case by mid morning and gone by early afternoon. We are a working kitchen, not a tasting room. The promise is simple: food you would actually eat at your desk, twelve dollars, nothing invented and nothing dressed up.
brand_identity.audience: Office workers 24 to 45 on a weekday lunch run with roughly eleven minutes to spend, buying on macros, speed and trust rather than on spectacle.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Twelve dollars a bowl, the everyday middle of grab and go. Above a supermarket meal deal, well below a chef counter. We are not a tasting menu and never pretend to be one.

brand_identity.typography: Ironwood Kitchen sets everything in Schibsted Grotesk and separates the levels by weight. The bowl name and its price share one baseline in Schibsted Grotesk Bold at 88 px on 96 px leading, tracked minus 0.020 em, one em apart, name in Ink Charcoal and figure in Salsa Clay. The closing line sets in Schibsted Grotesk Medium at 72 px on 80 px, tracked minus 0.015 em. The allergen and macro line sets in Schibsted Grotesk Regular at 28 px on 38 px with tracking at zero and no more than 65 characters a line, and fine print such as counter and route times sets in Schibsted Grotesk Regular at 20 px on 28 px, tracked plus 0.040 em. Case labels print names at 22 pt and body at 9 pt on 12 pt. The price is never printed smaller than the name.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, warm, counter honest, one thought per line. Example: "Twelve bucks, in the case by half ten, gone by two. That is the whole promise."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No brand kit survives. The wordmark exists only as a flat picture on a white ground, exported by a designer who has since left, with no vector file and no source anywhere. Everything else is a photograph or a spreadsheet.
brand_identity.values: Feed people well and tell the truth about what is in the bowl. The allergen line and the macros are not marketing, they are the deal.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: The bowl name and the price sit on one shared baseline at exactly the same size, name in Ink Charcoal and price in Salsa Clay one em apart, so the twelve dollars is drawn as large as the food it buys.

rules: Never print the price smaller than the name.
Name and price share one baseline at an identical size, exactly one em apart, never stacked and never in a badge.
The name sets in Ink Charcoal and the figure in Salsa Clay, never the reverse.
The whole package is one family, Schibsted Grotesk; the levels are carried by weight alone, Bold, Medium, Regular.
The allergen and macro line always runs at full contrast, never greyed back.
In print, case labels set names 22 pt and body 9 pt on 12 pt.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds and panels are Bench White or Field Green and nothing else. On Bench White, the bowl name, any closing line and body are Ink Charcoal, the price figure is Salsa Clay, the allergen line is Ink Charcoal or Field Green (as ironwood_linesheet_2027.pdf sets it; Field Green on Bench White counts as full contrast for the allergen line only), the macro figures are Ink Charcoal, and fine print may be Steel Grey. On Field Green, all type is Bench White, the ironwood_wordmark.png wordmark excepted. The bowl name and price line and the allergen and macro line always sit on Bench White. Salsa Clay covers the price figure alone and Steel Grey fine print alone. All on-screen type sits on a solid Bench White or Field Green ground or panel, never straight on footage or a still.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow, glow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour or type, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over footage or a still: type over a shot sits on a solid Bench White or Field Green panel. Cuts and short dissolves between shots are transitions, not tints; colour and opacity are judged on a settled frame.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, panels, rules, buttons or icons; the supplied footage, the bowl stills and the ironwood_wordmark.png letterforms are the only exceptions. No Steel Grey on the allergen and macro line. No badge, roundel or sticker behind the price. No outline, glow, drop shadow, gradient, bevel or metallic effect on any type or panel.
palette_rules.photography: The footage and the bowl stills keep their own colour and are never recoloured toward the palette; any correction keeps each dish's food colours true to life.
